newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed nuke start delayed to next week.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed nuke start delayed to next week.

text.p: Detroit Edison has delayed the planned startup of its 1,116 megawatt Fermi 2 nuclear power plant to next week following a maintenance and refueling outage, a company spokeswoman said Monday.
"It looks like it won't begin production until next week," said spokeswoman Mary Kay Bean.

The Monroe County, Mich. unit had originally been expected to restart near Nov 26, but that date had to be pushed back due to problems involving the electrical system on an emergency diesel generator, the spokeswoman said.
Fermi 2 was shut Sept 27 for the scheduled maintenance.

During the repair period, Detroit Edison planned to replace three turbines and upgrade the facility, although officials said the exact new generating capacity would not be known until the plant resumes operations.
Detroit Edison, a subsidiary of DTE Energy Co, has an overall generating capacity of 10,219 megawatts.
About 85 percent of the generation comes from coal-fired power plants, while the remainder comes mostly from Fermi 2.
